title: Principal-parts resolution of a vector bundle on a regular curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a nonempty integral Noetherian regular scheme of dimension one over $k$. Write $\eta$ for its generic point, $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field [def-sc-function-field], and $j:\{\eta\}\to X$. Let $E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], meaning Zariski-locally a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_X$, and put $V=E_\eta$. For every closed point $x$, identify $E_x$ with its image in $V$ and let $i_x:\{x\}\to X$. There is a natural exact sequence of Zariski sheaves
$$0\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow j_*V\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{x\text{ closed}}i_{x,*}(V/E_x)\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $(j_*V)(U)=V$ for nonempty open $U$ and is zero for $U=\varnothing$; the last map sends a rational section to its germs modulo $E_x$. Both sheaves after $E$ are flasque, meaning that all restriction maps on opens are surjective. In particular, every $v\in V$ is in $E_x$ for almost every closed $x$, and the connecting map in cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] gives
$$H^0(X,E)=\bigcap_{x\text{ closed}}E_x\subset V,\qquad H^1(X,E)\cong\operatorname{coker}\!\left(V\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{x\text{ closed}}V/E_x\right).$$
These identifications are natural for morphisms of finite locally free modules. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ and $E=\Omega^1_{X/k}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], then $V=\Omega^1_{K/k}$ and $E_x$ is the image of $\Omega^1_{\mathcal O_{X,x}/k}$ in $\Omega^1_{K/k}$.

proof.text: For a nonempty open $U$, every section of $E(U)$ has a generic germ in $V$, compatible with restriction; give $j_*V$ its $\mathcal O_X$-action through the generic germ of a function. On a trivializing neighbourhood $W$ from [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], the maps $E_x\to V$ and $E(W)\to V$ are the coordinatewise maps $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{r}\to K^{r}$ and $\mathcal O_X(W)^{r}\to K^{r}$. They are injective by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. For a section over any $U$ whose generic germ is zero, restrict to each trivializing $W\subseteq U$; its coordinates vanish by that same injectivity, so the sheaf axiom makes the section zero. This constructs the monomorphism $E\to j_*V$ and the stated inclusions $E_x\subseteq V$. Finite direct sums commute with taking germs because finitely many representatives can be restricted to their common neighbourhood.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: Every $v\in V=E_\eta$ is represented by a section over some neighbourhood $W$ of $\eta$, by the definition of a stalk. Thus $v\in E_x$ for all $x\in W$. By [lem-sc-nonempty-open-complement-finite-dim-le-one], $X\setminus W$ is finite; its hypotheses hold since an integral scheme is irreducible, sober and $T_0$, and the Noetherian scheme has Noetherian underlying space. Its points are closed by [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed]. More generally every $x\ne\eta$ is closed: $X\setminus\overline{\{x\}}$ is a nonempty open (otherwise $x$ would be the unique generic point), and the same closed-point lemma applies. Consequently the pole set of any $v$ is a finite set of closed points.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: Put $Q=\bigoplus_{x\text{ closed}}i_{x,*}(V/E_x)$, where the skyscraper has value $V/E_x$ on opens containing $x$ and zero on the other opens, with scalar action induced by $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Apply [lem-pur-module-sheaf-coproduct-local-support] on the site of opens of $X$ (intersections are its fibre products, and all indexing sets are taken in a fixed encompassing universe). It identifies $Q$ with the subsheaf of the product consisting of families locally supported on finitely many indices. Every open $U$ of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact, so a finite subcover of those neighbourhoods shows that a family in $Q(U)$ has globally finite support. Conversely every finitely supported family is locally finitely supported. Hence $Q(U)=\bigoplus_{x\in U,\ x\text{ closed}}V/E_x$, and restrictions discard coordinates. They are surjective by extension by zero. Restrictions of $j_*V$ between nonempty opens are identities of $V$, and restriction to the empty open is the map to zero. Thus both sheaves are flasque.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: For nonempty $U$, define $\delta_U(v)=(v\bmod E_x)_{x\in U,\ x\text{ closed}}$; step 2 makes its support finite. These maps commute with restriction and are $\mathcal O_X$-linear, since each $E_x$ is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-submodule. If $\delta_U(v)=0$, then $v\in E_x$ at every closed $x\in U$, and also at $\eta$ because $E_\eta=V$. By step 2 these are all points of $U$. At every $x$, membership in $E_x$ supplies a section $s_x$ on a neighbourhood of $x$ with generic germ $v$. On overlaps these sections agree by the injectivity proved in step 1, so they glue to a unique section of $E(U)$. Conversely every section of $E(U)$ has zero principal parts. Thus $E$ is the kernel of $\delta$; the unique lifts just constructed respect addition, scalar multiplication and restriction, so this is the kernel also in $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: To prove that $\delta:j_*V\to Q$ is an epimorphism, let $s\in Q(U)$. At a closed $x\in U$, choose $v\in V$ representing $s_x\in V/E_x$. The family $\delta_U(v)-s$ has finite support by steps 2 and 3, and its $x$-coordinate is zero. Delete its finitely many support points from $U$; they are closed and different from $x$, so this leaves a neighbourhood of $x$ on which $v$ lifts $s$. At $\eta$, delete the finite support of $s$; zero lifts $s$ on that neighbourhood. Thus the map on every stalk is surjective. By [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-epi-iff-stalk-epi] it is an epimorphism on underlying abelian sheaves, hence also on module sheaves: two module morphisms equal after composition with it have equal underlying abelian morphisms and are therefore equal. Together with steps 1 and 4 this gives the asserted short exact sequence.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-module-cup-flasque-acyclicity] to the two flasque module sheaves of step 3: their positive module cohomology vanishes. The long exact sequence of [pqf-def-cohomology], whose degree-zero terms are the global sections because $R^0\Gamma(X,-)\cong\Gamma(X,-)$ naturally by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], is therefore $0\to H^0(X,E)\to V\xrightarrow{\delta_X}\bigoplus_{x\text{ closed}}V/E_x\xrightarrow{\partial}H^1(X,E)\to0$. Its kernel is precisely the set of $v$ belonging to all $E_x$, and its cokernel is the displayed quotient by the image of $V$. Exactness gives the two asserted identifications, with the second induced by the connecting map.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: For a module morphism $f:E\to F$, its generic map $f_\eta:E_\eta\to F_\eta$ sends $E_x$ into $F_x$, since a local representative $s$ is sent to $f(s)$. It therefore induces maps on all quotients, with $[v]_x\mapsto[f_\eta(v)]_x$, and on their finite-support direct sums. The equality $\delta_F f_\eta(v)=([f_\eta(v)]_x)_x$ gives a morphism of the short exact sequences. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], connecting maps commute with every morphism of short exact sequences. This proves naturality of the cokernel identification; naturality of the intersection identification follows directly from $s_\eta\mapsto f_\eta(s_\eta)$.

source.place: §3, pp. 156–157, exact sequence before Theorem 4; §4, p. 157, divisor variant; explicit finite-locally-free extension of the local argument

proof.text: Suppose $X$ is smooth over $k$. By [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ is finite locally free, so the preceding argument applies to it. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identifies the sheaf with the sheaf associated to $\Omega_{A/k}$. Taking the stalk at the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $x$ gives $(\Omega_{A/k})_\mathfrak p$ by the definition of the associated module sheaf (germs are represented by $m/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] first with $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and then with all nonzero elements of the domain $A$ gives $E_x=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{X,x}/k}$ and $E_\eta=\Omega_{K/k}$. The maps of that node send $\mathrm da/s$ to $s^{-1}\mathrm d(a/1)$, so these identifications identify the generic-germ map with the canonical map $\Omega_{\mathcal O_{X,x}/k}\to\Omega_{K/k}$. Step 1 proves it injective; its image is exactly the lattice used in the statement.

I read the item and all 8 steps in full against every cited statement and against Tate §3 pp.156–157 and §4 p.157. Tate proves the case of O_X and divisor twists, with completed local fields and abelian sheaves. The item proves the finite-locally-free case with uncompleted quotients and module sheaves, and its proof is correctly marked agent-written. The statement is unchanged from base and there are no new nodes. The proof checks: step 1 gets injectivity of the generic-germ map from the trivializations and clause 2 of the integral-scheme leaf. Step 2 gets finite pole sets and shows every non-generic point is closed via uniqueness of generic points. Step 3 turns the locally finite support given by the coproduct lemma into globally finite support by quasi-compactness of opens, and both sheaves are flasque. Steps 4–5 prove the kernel by gluing (overlaps contain η) and stalkwise surjectivity, and an abelian epi is a module epi because the forgetful functor is faithful. Step 6 uses module flasque acyclicity, which is about the same module cohomology as pqf-def-cohomology. Step 7 gives naturality through a morphism of the short exact sequences and the δ-functor clause. Step 8 identifies the differential stalks with Ω_{O_x/k} and Ω_{K/k} by the localization node at A∖p and at A∖0. Small cases: rank 0, a DVR spectrum, A¹ (H¹=0 by partial fractions) and an imperfect k all agree with the statement. There is no duplicate: the closest nodes are regular-curve-divisor-calculus, the étale G_m divisor sequence and generic-kummer-residues, and none states this sequence for finite locally free modules. There is no cycle, no SGA citation, and live/side-live still have the item unsplit. The off-unit tool_uses are generic and I accept them.
